newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 96/97 capital spending plans up 9 pct-MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan 96/97 capital spending plans up 9 pct-MITI.

text.p: Japanese companies plan to invest a total of 17.9 trillion yen on plant and equipment during the current fiscal year to March 31, up nine percent from 1995/96 and the second straight year of increased spending, according to a Trade Ministry survey released on Friday.
The mid-October survey, which covered 1,450 large companies, showed the companies had not completed their capital spending plans for 1997/98.
But for now, planned capital spending for the year was down 1.8 percent from the estimated spending for the current fiscal year.
In 1996/97, capital spending in the manufacturing sector is expected to rise 10 percent, while it will go up 8.4 percent in the non-manufacturing sector, MITI said.
The ministry said companies are expected to increase their capital spending plans for 1997/98 if the economy continues to recover, but a substantial increase is unlikely.
